next_bottleneck_diagnosis.hypothesis_h2_v0_2: FUA-write amortization is the next lever. Per-transaction AG-DLM unlock pattern submits N FUA writes synchronously and waits for completion. Holding AG-DLM across multiple transactions (D10 yield quantum) would amortize write costs by N similarly to how the freshness bit amortizes read costs.

h2_partial_verdict.claim_v0_2: FUA-write amortization (skip per-trans drain when no peer is asking) is the dominant lever for cross-node metadata-create rsync.

h2_partial_verdict.verdict: PARTIAL — the lever is real, but naive skipping isn't the right policy.  The right policy is bounded yield quantum (D10): hold the cached AG-DLM for up to N transactions OR until BAST fires, whichever comes first.  N must be small enough that BAST drains complete before peer's CAW retries time out.

Re-bench at the chosen quantum value.  Acceptance: both test1 and test2 finish iter 1 with wall_s < 60 (H1 strict pass).
If yield quantum tunes well, set lazy_ag_drain default to 1 + quantum default to validated value, ship as v0.4.0.

t1_filesystem_shutdown_diagnosis.summary: test1 hit ETIMEDOUT on AG and inode DLM lock acquires, eventually triggering xfs_force_shutdown.  This is NOT in the v0.3.131 AG-DLM unlock code path; it is in the inode-DLM ilock_begin path which v6a phase 2 did not modify.
evidence: Shutdown trigger location: mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin+0x15c (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:1130) — the inode-lock path, not the AG-lock path.
All four DLM lock failures had rc=-110 (ETIMEDOUT) — peer's CAW grant did not arrive within the 120s CAW poll timeout.

test2 dmesg in the same time window (21:42-21:48) shows NO BAST events, NO failures, NO P39-INSTR markers.  test2 had finished its rsync at 21:39:54 and was idle, holding its cached AG-DLM and inode-DLM grants.  test1's BAST request to test2 either did not reach test2 or test2 did not act on it.

test1 was hard-rebooted (sysrq-b) before this run.  Hypothesis: test1's reboot left disklock / SCSI PR state that test2 still considered test1's; on test1's fresh mount, test2's view of test1 may have been out-of-sync.  D14 three-layer fencing and D15 journal replay should handle node death, but the path may not be exercised cleanly when the same node reboots and rejoins as itself.

This shutdown is EITHER (a) a race exposed by lazy_ag_drain holding cached state longer (giving more time for cluster-state divergence to manifest), OR (b) a pre-existing test1-reboot-recovery issue that would happen with knob=0 too.  Sess32 needs to disambiguate by re-running the bench after a CLEAN reset (no sysrq involved) to determine if the shutdown reproduces.

Architectural arc is validated; the residual test1 stability issue is the gating concern for default-on rollout.

rsync_bench_v0_3_132_q4.infra: Fresh cluster: virsh reset both test1 and test2; cluster_reset.sh; both nodes mounted multi-node; lazy_ag_drain=1 + ag_yield_quantum=4 set on both before bench.

test1.outcome: EIO + filesystem shutdown — SAME pattern as q=32.  Smaller quantum did NOT prevent the shutdown.

test2.outcome: CLEAN COMPLETION — all files match, md5 OK, no kernel errors

rsync_bench_v0_3_132_q4.verdict: Quantum size doesn't change the failure mode.  test1 fails identically at q=4 and q=32.  The bug is structural to the lazy_ag_drain=1 unlock path itself, not 'BAST drain takes too long because of accumulated dirty state'.  Smaller quantum slightly slows test2 (38.8s vs 26s at q=32) — expected because more eager drains.
interpretation_for_sess32: test2's clean completion at both q=32 and q=4 means the lazy path WORKS for the element-web workload.
test1's identical 360s shutdown at both q=32 and q=4 means the bug is NOT 'accumulated state too large' but something else that triggers reliably for the open-gpu workload.
Difference between test1 (open-gpu, 8137 files) and test2 (element-web, 4385 files) workloads — possibly file count, dir nesting depth, or specific access pattern triggers a code path bug.
OR difference between test1 (first-mounter, did mkfs) and test2 (joiner) roles — initial AG state may differ.

Sess32 must investigate by: (a) running test1 with element-web tree (swap workloads — does test1 still fail?); (b) running test2 with open-gpu tree (does test2 also fail with that workload?); (c) instrumenting the specific code path that hits ETIMEDOUT in mxfs_dlm_caw_lock.

Key suspicion: my v0.3.131/132 yield_remaining decrement is unprotected by some additional invariant.  Or the lazy_skip path has a subtle interaction with caw_wait_for_grant that doesn't trigger for fewer-files workloads.

solo_test_attempt.context: Sess31 also attempted test1 SOLO (single_node=true) with lazy=1 + open-gpu to distinguish cross-node bug from local bug.
solo_test_attempt.outcome: INCONCLUSIVE — test1 became SSH-unresponsive after ~28 min into the bench.  Pingable but FS hung.  Likely a wedge similar to the multi-node failure, suggesting the bug is NOT cross-node-specific — it's in test1's local lazy unlock path triggered by the open-gpu workload regardless of peer presence.
solo_test_attempt.implication: Narrows bug location.  The lazy_skip path has a structural bug that triggers with this workload's access pattern, independent of cross-node BAST coordination.  Sess32 should: (1) instrument every lazy_skip event and the immediately-following acquire to capture state at fail point, (2) try ag_yield_quantum=1 (only one skip per cycle) to determine if even single-skip causes the bug or only multi-skip accumulation.

mxfs_v5_v0_3_132_solo_q1_breakthrough.context: After q=4 reproduced test1 shutdown identically to q=32 (proving accumulation-size doesn't matter), sess31 ran the prescribed q=1 SOLO test as the next diagnostic step.
mxfs_v5_v0_3_132_solo_q1_breakthrough.setup: test1 freshly virsh-reset.  Brought up SOLO (no test2 mount).  mxfs.ko v0.3.132 loaded.  mkfs_mxfs -f, mounted single-node.  dmesg confirmed single_node=true.  lazy_ag_drain=1, ag_yield_quantum=1.
mxfs_v5_v0_3_132_solo_q1_breakthrough.workload: rsync -a /root/open-gpu-kernel-modules/ /mnt/shared/test1_solo_q1_open_gpu/ (8137 files, 584 MB), then sudo sync.

result.outcome: BREAKTHROUGH — within 30% of native XFS performance on the metadata-heavy create workload that was originally DNF after 9+ minutes.

but_post_write_reads_hang.observation: The bench script's subsequent `find /mnt/shared/test1_solo_q1_open_gpu -type f | wc -l` hung test1's SSH responsiveness.  Pingable but command-unresponsive.
but_post_write_reads_hang.implication: Bug is NOT in the write path.  rsync (which is mostly writes for this workload) completed correctly in 4 seconds.  The bug surfaces during read-back operations on the freshly-written tree.  The earlier 360s shutdowns are now consistent with this: they begin with `rsync: cannot stat destination` (a READ, not a write) — same root cause.
but_post_write_reads_hang.sess32_diagnostic_target: Why do post-lazy-unlock reads (via find/stat/lookup) eventually trigger ino=128 ETIMEDOUT and shutdown?  Possible: (a) lazy_skip leaves pag_mxfs_alloc_dirty set with nontrivial state that some inode-side check reads and treats as 'must wait for drain'; (b) freshness-bit (_XBF_FUA_FRESH) interacts with lazy-unlocked AG metadata such that reads see stale-but-marked-fresh content; (c) the inode-DLM caw_lock path in single_node mode has an edge case that lazy AG state exposes.

mxfs_v5_v0_3_135_cil_flush_fix.session: sess31 final fix attempt: CIL push hypothesis
mxfs_v5_v0_3_135_cil_flush_fix.fix_description: Add unconditional xfs_log_force(mp, 0) at end of mxfs_ag_dlm_unlock holders==0 transition under lazy_ag_drain=1.  Forces CIL push on every unlock, keeping btree-block BLI items unpinned so xfsaild can push them and log tail advances.  ~5 LOC change.
mxfs_v5_v0_3_135_cil_flush_fix.rationale: Pre-fix diagnosis: most file-create transactions don't allocate new inode chunks (use existing free inodes from inobt).  v0.3.133/134 fixes only fired drain on alloc_dirty branch, which most trans don't reach.  Btree-block BLI items pinned by unflushed CIL records → xfsaild stuck → log fills → xlog_grant_head_wait wedges.

result.outcome: FIX VERIFIED on single-node — write phase + post-write reads both clean, no wedge, no log starvation

rsync_bench_v0_3_135_solo.vs_native_xfs: 12.14 / 3.12 = 3.9x XFS native (FULL workload including post-write reads)

test1.outcome: SHUTDOWN — disk lock acquisition timed out after 120000 ms (DIFFERENT error mode from prior runs — was AG-DLM timeout, now disklock heartbeat timeout)

rsync_bench_v0_3_135_multi.interpretation: Single-node fix works.  Multi-node has SEPARATE bug (disklock heartbeat timeout instead of AG-DLM timeout) that was previously masked by log starvation.  Sess32 needs to debug this disklock timeout specifically.
